title: Nuevo Laredo’s Festival de la Catrina draws more than 3,500 to downtown for Día de Muertos
excerpt: More than 3,500 people filled downtown Nuevo Laredo on November 1 for the Festival de la Catrina 2026, with a Catrina parade, art, music and food.
content:
More than 3,500 people filled downtown Nuevo Laredo on Saturday, November 1, for the Festival de la Catrina 2026, a municipal celebration of Día de Muertos that turned the city center into a parade route of color, music and tradition, according to local reporting.

The celebration began with the traditional Desfile de Catrinas, which moved through downtown streets to the beat of a batucada, according to Eleese Noticias. The program that followed featured artistic presentations, including a tribute to singer Viola Trigo, along with Catrina contests and an exhibition of Altares de Muertos honoring the holiday’s traditions.

Food stalls, Day of the Dead goods and local merchants, artisans and vendors were part of the day as well, giving families a place to eat, shop and gather while the festival unfolded, local reporting said. The municipal government organized the festival, and city leaders said events like it are meant to give families shared public spaces and keep the region’s traditions alive.

The festival has become one of the events that mark Nuevo Laredo’s Día de Muertos season, drawing families downtown for art, music, food and remembrance.
